note: PI3K-pathway-driven breast lines and xenografts predicted pan-PI3K activity and PIK3CA-mutant enrichment; pictilisib's randomised trials missed PFS with no mutant enrichment, buparlisib's two fulvestrant phase 3s won by about two months and were abandoned for liver and mood toxicity the models never flagged.
label: Breast cancer (pan-PI3K)

engagement.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4, MDA-MB-361)
engagement.note: GDC-0941 at 150 mg/kg held tumour exposure above antiproliferative levels for >8 h with sustained pathway (pAkt) inhibition in xenografts.
engagement.short: Sustained pAkt inhibition in xenograft tumours
engagement.quote: GDC-0941 showed comparable in vitro antitumor activity to PI-103, PI-540, and PI-620 and exhibited 78% oral bioavailability in mice, with tumor exposure above 50% antiproliferative concentrations for >8 hours following 150 mg/kg p.o. and sustained phosphatidylinositide 3-kinase pathway inhibition.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMC2718129 open access). Pivotal preclinical paper for pictilisib; glioblastoma and ovarian xenografts, breast models came with O'Brien 2010.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at first use for the class: the model's PD readout is tumour PI3K-pathway (pAkt) inhibition at an exposure above the antiproliferative concentration.

engagement.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4, MDA-MB-361)
engagement.note: Pictilisib suppressed tumour Ser473-pAkt >90% at exposures above 20 h·µmol/L and PRP pAkt >90% at the MTD; insulin, glucose and FDG-PET moved.
engagement.quote: Levels of phosphorylated serine-473 AKT were suppressed >90% in PRP at 3 hours after dose at the MTD and in tumor at pictilisib doses associated with AUC >20 h·μmol/L.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMC4287394 open access). Mixed solid-tumour phase 1 (n=60), not breast-specific; phase 1 NCT not located, so registry_date is null. Full text states the comparison itself (preclinical PK reproduced; MDA-MB-361 PK-PD target AUC reached; effects 'not exactly reproduced'), so comparison_stated true and source_calls_it partial.
engagement.magnitude_basis: tumour pAkt suppression; the model abstract states sustained pathway inhibition without a percentage, patients >90%
engagement.reason: Tumour pAkt suppressed in dosed patients
engagement.judgement: The model's readout (tumour pAkt) moved in dosed humans, so same; the trial is in mixed solid tumours, which the brief allows for engagement. Every member concurs: pilaralisib cut tumour and surrogate pAKT/S6 40-80% (Shapiro 2014, doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-13-1777, epub 2013), buparlisib moved skin pS6, C-peptide and FDG-PET dose-dependently (Bendell 2012, doi 10.1200/JCO.2011.36.1360), and in ER+ breast patients pictilisib plus anastrozole suppressed Ki-67 more than anastrozole alone (OPPORTUNE, Schmid 2016, doi 10.1200/JCO.2015.63.9179; downstream). Scored on Sarker 2015 because its model side (Raynaud 2009, same ICR group) is the pivotal preclinical paper; Shapiro 2014 is a year earlier but its model paper (Foster 2015) was published after the trial.

dose.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4, MDA-MB-361)
dose.note: Exposure target stated: tumour concentration above the 50% antiproliferative level for >8 h after 150 mg/kg oral; no tolerability margin stated. Full text also calls 150 mg/kg 'well tolerated'; that passing tolerability claim is scored once, in safety.
dose.quote: GDC-0941 showed comparable in vitro antitumor activity to PI-103, PI-540, and PI-620 and exhibited 78% oral bioavailability in mice, with tumor exposure above 50% antiproliferative concentrations for >8 hours following 150 mg/kg p.o. and sustained phosphatidylinositide 3-kinase pathway inhibition.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The abstract reports no body-weight, NOAEL or tolerated-dose statement for mice.
dose.judgement: Opening entry: the model gives an exposure target (tumour level above the antiproliferative concentration with sustained pathway inhibition) but no tolerability margin, so decision 16 cannot be applied on this track.

dose.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4, MDA-MB-361)
dose.note: Sarker states the MDA-MB-361 xenograft PK-PD model's target, AUC 6 h·µM for ≥90% growth inhibition, was reached in most patients above 80 mg.
dose.quote: predicted the minimal target plasma AUC to be 6uM*hr (3000 ng*hr/ml) in order to achieve ≥90% tumor growth inhibition; this target AUC was achieved in most patients treated at doses >80mg
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC4287394). The MDA-MB-361 target is stated in-source without a citation of its own (ref 9 is Raynaud 2009, U87MG and IGROV-1; Salphati 2010, doi 10.1124/dmd.110.032912, modelled MCF7.1), so model_src is null and the comparison is Sarker's own. Replaces the FERGI pairing, whose note read platelet-rich-plasma pAkt (>90% at the 330 mg MTD) as tumour pAkt (>90% only at AUC >20 h·µM). Pictilisib phase 1 results are not posted on ClinicalTrials.gov, so registry_date is null. margin_stated stays false pending the open Decision 16 rule question on Raynaud's 'very well tolerated' claim.
dose.magnitude_basis: threshold exposure (plasma AUC 6 h·µM) reached at doses >80 mg; the trials dosed 260-340 mg
dose.population: Advanced solid tumours, pictilisib monotherapy phase 1 (Sarker 2015)
dose.reason: Model's exposure target reached in most patients
dose.judgement: Dose asks whether the model's stated exposure target was reached. Sarker states the target (minimal plasma AUC 6 h·µM for ≥90% growth inhibition of MDA-MB-361, a HER2-amplified, PIK3CA-mutant breast xenograft) and that most patients above 80 mg reached it: same, comparison stated. Whether that exposure worked is efficacy, contra on this track for pictilisib. Tumour pAkt fell >90% only above AUC 20 h·µM (2 of 3 biopsied patients), more than three times the target, so the target was low for pathway blockade in patients' tumours; but the 330 mg MTD gave a mean AUC near 23 h·µM in the phase 1, FERGI's 340 mg sat at that exposure and still missed, so no higher dose later worked and the 'target too low' row does not apply. The model's HER2-amplified tumour against FERGI's HER2-negative patients bears on efficacy, not on whether the exposure was reached.

efficacy.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4, MDA-MB-361)
efficacy.note: Breast lines and xenografts with PIK3CA mutation, HER2 amplification or dual pathway lesions were exquisitely sensitive to GDC-0941; some unaltered models responded too. Opener year is pictilisib's own first use of this xenograft system, Raynaud 2009 (PMID 19584227, epub 2009-07-07), as in the engagement, dose and safety openers; O'Brien 2010 is the breast-specific source.
efficacy.quote: We found that models harboring mutations in PIK3CA, amplification of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2, or dual alterations in two pathway components were exquisitely sensitive to the antitumor effects of GDC-0941.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. First breast-specific model paper for a member; Wallin 2012 (doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-11-2088) added breast xenografts and PDX with docetaxel, Sanchez 2011 (doi 10.1186/bcr2833) BKM120 with oestrogen deprivation in ER+ lines in vitro.
efficacy.population: breast cancer lines and xenografts, PI3K-pathway-altered and unaltered
efficacy.judgement: Class-level opening entry in the breast models (the track's first use was Raynaud 2009 in non-breast xenografts, proxy allowed).

efficacy.model: Breast cancer cell-line panel with genotype: PIK3CA-mutant and HER2-amplified lines most sensitive
efficacy.note: Pharmacogenomic profiling of a large breast-line panel proposed PIK3CA mutation, HER2 amplification and a gene signature to pick responders.
efficacy.short: PIK3CA/HER2 status proposed to pick responders
efficacy.quote: Pathway focused biomarkers and the gene expression signature described in this study may have utility in the identification of patients likely to benefit from therapy with a selective PI3K inhibitor.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Maira 2012 (doi 10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-11-0474) made the same prediction for buparlisib from a 353-line panel (preferential inhibition of PIK3CA-mutant lines).
efficacy.judgement: A separate track: a different prediction (which patients respond) from a genotype-annotated line panel, not the class-level xenograft question. model_kind is animal because the panel paper also carried xenografts; the genotype call itself is in vitro.

efficacy.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4, MDA-MB-361)
efficacy.note: FERGI: pictilisib plus fulvestrant did not improve PFS (6.6 vs 5.1 months, HR 0.74, p=0.096) in AI-resistant ER+ breast cancer. Combination with fulvestrant, scored on its PFS primary. Dated to SABCS December 2014. Buparlisib now has its own track on this model.
efficacy.quote: In part 1, we found no difference in median progression-free survival between the pictilisib (6·6 months [95% CI 3·9-9·8]) and placebo (5·1 months [3·6-7·3]) group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·74 [95% CI 0·52-1·06]; p=0·096).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMC5524539). NCT01437566 has no results posted; year is the 2016-05-04 epub. BELLE-2 was presented at SABCS 2015 but its first admissible record is the 2017 paper. Year moved to 2014: FERGI part 1 was presented at SABCS in December 2014 (AACR blog 2014-12-12, 'did not benefit others'; not statistically significant).

patient_trials.quote: In the ITT population, the median PFS was 8.2 months with pictilisib (n = 91) versus 7.8 months with placebo (n = 92) [hazard ratio (HR) for progression or death, 0.95; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.62-1.46; P = 0.83].

In the total patient population (n=1147), median progression-free survival was 6·9 months (95% CI 6·8-7·8) in the buparlisib group versus 5·0 months (4·0-5·2) in the placebo group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·78 [95% CI 0·67-0·89]; one-sided p=0·00021).

Median progression-free survival was significantly longer in the buparlisib versus placebo group (3·9 months [95% CI 2·8-4·2] vs 1·8 months [1·5-2·8]; hazard ratio [HR] 0·67, 95% CI 0·53-0·84, one-sided p=0·00030).

At adaptive interim analysis, there was no improvement in PFS with buparlisib versus placebo in the full (median PFS 8.0 versus 9.2 months, hazard ratio [HR] 1.18), or PI3K pathway-activated population (median PFS 9.1 versus 9.2 months, HR 1.17).
Overall, pCR rate was similar between buparlisib and placebo arms (32.0% versus 40%; one-sided P = 0.811).
Fifty-one patients were enrolled in phase II; one patient had a partial response in the pilaralisib arm.
No responses occurred in Arm 1; four of 20 evaluable patients (20 %) in Arm 2 had a partial response.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft growth inhibition versus PFS HR 0.74, p=0.096 (not significant)
efficacy.reason: Pictilisib failed; buparlisib wins cannot flip
efficacy.judgement: Pictilisib track: pictilisib plus fulvestrant missed its PFS primary in FERGI (SABCS 2014; paper 2016) and PEGGY, so contra. Buparlisib, whose patients differed in result (BELLE-2 and BELLE-3 met PFS primaries), is split onto its own track, appended at the end of this cell. Pilaralisib (1 PR of 51 with letrozole) agrees with pictilisib and gets no separate track. OPPORTUNE (Ki-67 primary) is a PD window study, scored under engagement.

efficacy.model: Breast cancer cell-line panel with genotype: PIK3CA-mutant and HER2-amplified lines most sensitive
efficacy.note: FERGI: PIK3CA-mutant patients gained nothing over wild-type (HR 0.73 vs 0.72), and the mutant-only part 2 showed HR 1.07. Dated to SABCS December 2014, where PIK3CA status was reported as not predictive.
efficacy.short: PIK3CA mutation did not enrich benefit
efficacy.quote: We also found no difference when patients were analysed according to presence (pictilisib 6·5 months [95% CI 3·7-9·8] vs placebo 5·1 months [2·6-10·4]; HR 0·73 [95% CI 0·42-1·28]; p=0·268)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Quote is a verbatim leading fragment of the abstract's PIK3CA sentence. Same-year earlier signals: OPPORTUNE (epub 2016-03-14) found PIK3CA mutations not predictive of Ki-67 response, and the buparlisib phase 1s (Bendell 2012, Rodon 2014) saw no correlation of tumour molecular status with benefit. Year moved to 2014: at SABCS 2014 Krop said PIK3CA mutation 'was not predictive of benefit from pictilisib' (AACR blog 2014-12-12).

patient_trials.quote: In patients with PIK3CA-mutated tumours, the median PFS was 7.3 months for pictilisib (n = 32) versus 5.8 months with placebo (n = 30) (HR, 1.06; 95% CI 0.52-2.12; P = 0.88).

In PI3K pathway-activated patients (n=372), median progression-free survival was 6·8 months (95% CI 4·9-7·1) in the buparlisib group versus 4·0 months (3·1-5·2) in the placebo group (HR 0·76 [0·60-0·97], one-sided p=0·014).
There was no association between molecular alterations in the PI3K pathway and efficacy.
Observed PIK3CA mutations in cell-free circulating DNA did not correlate with response.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PFS HR 0.73 in PIK3CA-mutant versus 0.72 in wild-type: no enrichment
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level prediction tested on its own drug: the panel said PIK3CA-mutant tumours are exquisitely sensitive, and the stratified, then mutant-only, FERGI showed no enrichment. PEGGY (HR 1.06 mutant), pilaralisib (no association, two trials) and BELLE-4 (HR 1.17 pathway-activated) agree. BELLE-2's tissue-defined pathway-activated group (HR 0.76 vs 0.78 overall) adds nothing, and its ctDNA PIK3CA-mutant exploratory signal (HR 0.56) and BELLE-3's are partial matches on another drug that cannot flip a contra track.

efficacy.model: Breast cancer patient-derived tumour xenograft (PDTX) biobank with short-term PDTX-derived tumour cell (PDTC) ex vivo drug screen (Cambridge; pictilisib ex vivo, buparlisib in vivo)
efficacy.note: PDTC screen of pictilisib across 15 models: sensitivity sat with PIK3CA-activating mutation, PTEN loss, INPP4B loss or high p-AKT; buparlisib dosed in PDTXs in vivo.
efficacy.short: PDTC screen ties pictilisib sensitivity to PIK3CA/PTEN
efficacy.quote: Sensitivity to the PI3Kα inhibitor GDC00941 (pictilisib) was seen in models with PIK3CA-activating mutations (3/15), PTEN loss (5/15), INPP4B loss (2/15), high p-AKT levels (4/15), or a combination of these features
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5037319, open access). The paper pairs no PI3K-inhibitor result with a patient: the biobank's patients were not treated with class members. model_kind is ex_vivo because the scored pictilisib screen is in PDTCs; the same biobank also dosed buparlisib in PDTXs in vivo (Table S7, numbers not quotable from the text).
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the biobank's first published use. Patient-level prediction (which genotypes respond to pictilisib); the paper itself makes no comparison with patients.
efficacy.population: Breast cancer PDTX/PDTC models (n = 15 screened with pictilisib), ER+ and ER- mixed

efficacy.model: Breast cancer patient-derived tumour xenograft (PDTX) biobank with short-term PDTX-derived tumour cell (PDTC) ex vivo drug screen (Cambridge; pictilisib ex vivo, buparlisib in vivo)
efficacy.note: PDTCs said PIK3CA-mutant tumours respond better to pictilisib; FERGI's PIK3CA-mutant patients gained nothing over wild-type (HR 0.73 vs 0.72) and PEGGY agreed (HR 1.06). Retrodiction: the biobank was first public (Sept 2016) after FERGI's PIK3CA result (Dec 2014), and failed to reproduce it, so contra.
efficacy.short: PIK3CA-mutant enrichment not seen in FERGI
efficacy.quote: We also found no difference when patients were analysed according to presence (pictilisib 6·5 months [95% CI 3·7-9·8] vs placebo 5·1 months [2·6-10·4]; HR 0·73 [95% CI 0·42-1·28]; p=0·268)
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by us: Bruna 2016 full text (model side, 'models with mutant versus wild-type PIK3CA responded better to PI3Kα and AKT inhibitors') against the FERGI paper (abstract-level; PMC5524539). Dating: FERGI was public before Bruna (SABCS 2014; epub 2016-05-04 vs 2016-09-15), but Bruna does not cite FERGI and the screen date is not stated, so retrodiction is left false; the status is contra under either reading. NCT01437566 has no results posted.
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level prediction tested on its own drug: the ex-vivo screen put pictilisib sensitivity with PIK3CA mutation and PTEN loss; the stratified, then mutant-only, FERGI showed no enrichment, and PEGGY (HR 1.06) agreed. BELLE-2's tissue-defined PI3K-pathway-activated group (HR 0.76 vs 0.78 overall) adds nothing for buparlisib, and its ctDNA PIK3CA signal is a partial match on another drug that cannot flip a contra track. One drug's contra beats another's same on the same track. Under the retrodiction rule post-dating alone makes this a retrodiction (FERGI's PIK3CA result was public at SABCS 2014 for the same target); it failed to reproduce the patient result, so it stays contra with retrodiction true.
efficacy.reason: Ex-vivo genotype call missed in patients

patient_trials.quote: In patients with PIK3CA-mutated tumours, the median PFS was 7.3 months for pictilisib (n = 32) versus 5.8 months with placebo (n = 30) (HR, 1.06; 95% CI 0.52-2.12; P = 0.88).

In PI3K pathway-activated patients (n=372), median progression-free survival was 6·8 months (95% CI 4·9-7·1) in the buparlisib group versus 4·0 months (3·1-5·2) in the placebo group (HR 0·76 [0·60-0·97], one-sided p=0·014).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PFS HR 0.73 in PIK3CA-mutant versus 0.72 in wild-type (FERGI part 1), HR 1.07 in the mutant-only part 2: no enrichment
efficacy.population: ER+/HER2-negative, aromatase-inhibitor-resistant advanced breast cancer; PIK3CA-mutant versus wild-type (FERGI, PEGGY)

efficacy.model: Novartis PDX Encyclopedia 1x1x1 'PDX clinical trial' (~1,000 PDXs, six indications; buparlisib-treated PDXs stratified by PAM50 luminal A, PIK3CA and MAP3K1 status)
efficacy.note: Population-scale PDX screen of 62 treatments, buparlisib among them, built to predict clinical trial response; no breast-cancer pan-PI3K comparison verifiable from the abstract.
efficacy.short: PDX 'clinical trial' built to predict response
efficacy.quote: We demonstrate both the reproducibility and the clinical translatability of this approach by identifying associations between a genotype and drug response, and established mechanisms of resistance.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading: nature.com redirects to login and the Firecrawl scrape returned only abstract and references, so whether Gao 2015 itself pairs BKM120 breast-PDX responses with a trial is unverified. Buparlisib's place in the screen is confirmed by Nixon 2019, which analyses 170 buparlisib-treated PDXs from this database (its reference 22).
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the PDX encyclopedia's first published use; the first verifiable comparison for a class member in breast cancer comes in Nixon 2019.
efficacy.population: PDXs across six solid-tumour indications including breast; buparlisib single agent

efficacy.model: Novartis PDX Encyclopedia 1x1x1 'PDX clinical trial' (~1,000 PDXs, six indications; buparlisib-treated PDXs stratified by PAM50 luminal A, PIK3CA and MAP3K1 status)
efficacy.note: After luminal A tracked with clinical benefit on buparlisib + letrozole, the 170 buparlisib-treated PDXs were re-stratified: luminal A predicted response; PIK3CA mutation did not, matching the clinic. Combination with letrozole in a phase Ib.
efficacy.short: PDX re-analysis reproduces luminal A benefit
efficacy.quote: However, luminal A status predicted response to both drugs, albeit with a greater number of PDXs harboring luminal A gene expression than having alterations in PIK3CA or MAP3K1.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6757060, open access). Weak on both sides: 14 buparlisib patient tumours with PAM50 (3/3 with clinical benefit luminal A), significance only as a trend (p = 0.07) pooled with alpelisib, which is not a class member; the 170 PDXs span solid-tumour types, not breast alone, with n = 1 per model. NCT01248494 has no results posted.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: the luminal A hypothesis came from the patients and the PDX database was then queried 'to provide additional evidence', so the model was run against a known answer. It reproduced the direction (luminal A better on buparlisib) and also reproduced the PIK3CA non-enrichment ('PDXs with MAP3K1 alterations were more sensitive to alpelisib ... but not buparlisib'; PIK3CA-mutant PDXs trended only for alpelisib), consistent with FERGI, PEGGY and BELLE-2 tissue results. Scored retro, not same; counted apart.
efficacy.reason: Model reran against known clinic answer

patient_trials.quote: Interestingly, all three patients with clinical benefit to buparlisib/letrozole had a luminal A-like gene expression pattern in their cancer.
Patients harboring mutations in both genes exhibited the greatest likelihood of clinical benefit.

In PI3K pathway-activated patients (n=372), median progression-free survival was 6·8 months (95% CI 4·9-7·1) in the buparlisib group versus 4·0 months (3·1-5·2) in the placebo group (HR 0·76 [0·60-0·97], one-sided p=0·014).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PDX day-28 tumour-volume change by luminal A status versus clinical benefit rate (CR/PR or SD >= 6 months) by luminal A status on buparlisib + letrozole
efficacy.population: ER+/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer on buparlisib + letrozole phase Ib (NCT01248494), n = 14 with PAM50 subtype; PDX panel across solid-tumour types

efficacy.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4, MDA-MB-361)
efficacy.quote: NVP-BKM120 shows dose-dependent in vivo pharmacodynamic activity as measured by significant inhibition of p-Akt and tumor growth inhibition in mechanistic xenograft models.
efficacy.note: Buparlisib's first use of the xenograft system: p-Akt inhibition and growth inhibition in mechanistic xenografts.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry for buparlisib's track on this model, split off because buparlisib's patients differed in result from pictilisib's.
efficacy.population: mechanistic xenografts (A2780, U87MG) and a 353-line panel

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PFS gain of 1.9 months (HR 0.78) against the model's xenograft growth inhibition
efficacy.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4, MDA-MB-361)
efficacy.quote: In the total patient population (n=1147), median progression-free survival was 6·9 months (95% CI 6·8-7·8) in the buparlisib group versus 5·0 months (4·0-5·2) in the placebo group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·78 [95% CI 0·67-0·89]; one-sided p=0·00021).
efficacy.note: BELLE-2: buparlisib plus fulvestrant met its PFS primary (6.9 vs 5.0 months, HR 0.78). Combination with fulvestrant, scored like any trial; dated to SABCS December 2015.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMC5549667). Year is the SABCS 2015 presentation (abstract S6-01, 2015-12-11, ASCO Post report); the 2017 paper is the quoted source. Model side is Maira 2012 (xenografts, not breast-specific).
efficacy.judgement: Split from the pictilisib track because buparlisib's patients differed in result. The model predicted activity; BELLE-2 (and BELLE-3, HR 0.67) met PFS primaries, a modest gain the authors call 'modest', so same with source_calls_it partial. BELLE-4 (paclitaxel, futility) enrolled HER2-negative patients regardless of hormone receptor status, so it sits outside the tile's HR-positive population and in patient_trials only.

patient_trials.quote: Median progression-free survival was significantly longer in the buparlisib versus placebo group (3·9 months [95% CI 2·8-4·2] vs 1·8 months [1·5-2·8]; hazard ratio [HR] 0·67, 95% CI 0·53-0·84, one-sided p=0·00030).

At adaptive interim analysis, there was no improvement in PFS with buparlisib versus placebo in the full (median PFS 8.0 versus 9.2 months, hazard ratio [HR] 1.18), or PI3K pathway-activated population (median PFS 9.1 versus 9.2 months, HR 1.17).

efficacy.model: Cancer cell-line panel with genotype (353 lines, Novartis): PIK3CA-mutant lines preferentially inhibited by buparlisib
efficacy.note: Maira 2012's 353-line panel found buparlisib preferentially inhibited PIK3CA-mutant tumour cells, not KRAS- or PTEN-mutant ones.
efficacy.quote: Tested in a panel of 353 cell lines, NVP-BKM120 exhibited preferential inhibition of tumor cells bearing PIK3CA mutations, in contrast to either KRAS or PTEN mutant models.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 22188813, epub 2011-12-21). model_kind animal follows the pictilisib panel track: the paper also carried xenografts; the genotype call itself is in vitro.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry of buparlisib's own patient-level genotype track (checker 'missing' item); a different system and drug from Genentech's breast-line panel for pictilisib.

efficacy.model: Cancer cell-line panel with genotype (353 lines, Novartis): PIK3CA-mutant lines preferentially inhibited by buparlisib
efficacy.note: BELLE-2's co-primary in tissue PI3K-pathway-activated patients missed its one-sided 0.01 bar (HR 0.76, against 0.78 overall); combination with fulvestrant.
efficacy.quote: in the PI3K pathway-activated group (n=372 [n=188 in the buparlisib group and n=184 in the placebo group]), there was no significant difference in progression-free survival between the groups according to predefined criteria at one-sided α=0·01
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5549667). The co-primary population was PI3K pathway-activated in tissue (PIK3CA mutation or PTEN loss), wider than the panel's PIK3CA call. PFS by ctDNA PIK3CA status was a prespecified exploratory endpoint (benefit with mutant, not non-mutant, ctDNA), so it sits in patient_trials and changes no status. Dated to SABCS 2015 (abstract S6-01), where the activated group did not meet its planned endpoint.

patient_trials.quote: A significant difference in progression-free survival in the buparlisib group versus the placebo group was recorded in patients with ctDNA PIK3CA mutations (figure 3A), but not those with non-mutant ctDNA (figure 3B).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PFS HR 0.76 in the tissue PI3K-activated co-primary versus 0.78 in all patients: no enrichment
efficacy.population: PI3K pathway-activated (tissue PIK3CA mutation or PTEN loss), HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer after an aromatase inhibitor (BELLE-2)
efficacy.judgement: The panel predicted that PIK3CA-mutant tumours respond best to buparlisib. BELLE-2 tested that prospectively as a co-primary in the tissue-defined PI3K-activated population, which missed its predefined one-sided 0.01 bar and showed no enrichment over the whole trial (HR 0.76 vs 0.78): contra, scored on the co-primary that carries the prediction. The ctDNA PIK3CA-mutant benefit (prespecified exploratory) points the panel's way but is not an endpoint the rules score, so it sits in patient_trials. Not a retrodiction: Maira 2012 (December 2011) predates FERGI's genotype result (December 2014) and BELLE-2 (December 2015).

safety.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4, MDA-MB-361)
safety.note: Mice dosed 150 mg/kg daily to 98% growth inhibition; the abstract makes no tolerability statement. Full text states the effective dose was well tolerated; that passing tolerability claim is this track's safety prediction.
safety.quote: These properties led to excellent dose-dependent oral antitumor activity, with daily p.o. dosing at 150 mg/kg achieving 98% and 80% growth inhibition of U87MG glioblastoma and IGROV-1 ovarian cancer xenografts, respectively.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no body-weight, glucose or toxicity statement in the abstract.
safety.judgement: Opening entry: Raynaud's full text says the therapy was well tolerated with normal weight gain at the effective dose, a passing tolerability claim now scored as a safety prediction (compared in the appended pictilisib entry).

safety.model: Novartis rat and dog toxicology and safety pharmacology of buparlisib (the package behind its 2008 first-in-human trial)
safety.note: Novartis called buparlisib's preclinical safety profile supportive; its rat and dog package preceded the November 2008 first-in-human trial.
safety.quote: The pharmacological, biologic, and preclinical safety profile of NVP-BKM120 supports its clinical development and the compound is undergoing phase II clinical trials in patients with cancer.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Maira 2012 (PMID 22188813, epub 2011-12-21). The package's contents are known from Novartis' BERIL-1 protocol (NCT01852292, Prot_001.pdf, version 03 dated 2016-08-30, uploaded to ClinicalTrials.gov 2018-03-30).
safety.judgement: Re-homed from the xenograft track: the 'preclinical safety profile' Maira 2012 cites is the rat and dog toxicology package, not the xenografts (checker, safety 2). Opens at buparlisib's first use of the package, proxied by the first-in-human start (CBKM120X2101, NCT01068483, started 2008-11); Maira 2012 is its first public statement, a passing tolerability claim scored as a safety prediction.

safety.model: Novartis rat and dog toxicology and safety pharmacology of buparlisib (the package behind its 2008 first-in-human trial)
safety.note: BELLE-2: grade 3-4 ALT 25% vs 1%; depression and anxiety more common. Rat/dog package showed no liver finding and no behavioural effect.
safety.short: Liver and mood harms missed by rat/dog tox
safety.quote: The most common grade 3-4 adverse events in the buparlisib group versus the placebo group were increased alanine aminotransferase (146 [25%] of 573 patients vs six [1%] of 570), increased aspartate aminotransferase (103 [18%] vs 16 [3%])
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5549667): 'The most frequently reported mood disorders were depression and anxiety, and these were more common in the buparlisib group than in the placebo group'. Model side verified from the BERIL-1 protocol (NCT01852292, Prot_001.pdf, version 03 dated 2016-08-30, uploaded 2018-03-30): 'Safety pharmacology studies in rats revealed no effects on neuronal (behavior) or respiratory functions.' The protocol is a sponsor document on a registry record, so it verifies the package but does not date the entry; the 2015 status rests on Maira 2012's claim. Year 2014 (checker): the phase 1b of buparlisib with letrozole in ER+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer (Mayer 2014, J Clin Oncol, PMID 24663045, epub March 2014) already reported transaminitis and mood disorders among drug-related events; BELLE-2 (SABCS 2015, abstract S6-01) is the placebo-controlled, higher-tier source. NCT01610284 results posted 2020-06-18.
safety.reason: Rat/dog tox missed liver and mood harms
safety.judgement: Scored on harms the species could have shown. Novartis' rat and dog package, summarised in the BERIL-1 protocol, lists lymphoid and erythroid depletion, pancreatic, male reproductive and glucose findings and no liver finding, and rat safety pharmacology found no behavioural effect. In BELLE-2 grade 3-4 ALT rises hit a quarter of patients and depression and anxiety were more common on buparlisib; ALT, AST and depression led the discontinuations, and no further studies were pursued owing to toxicity. Mood, unscored while this claim sat on the xenograft track, is scored here because the package tested rat behaviour; the rats' shifts in brain neurotransmitters carried no behavioural or mood prediction. Hyperglycaemia is on-target and the package showed it (glucose homeostasis affected in mice, rats and dogs), so it is not a miss. Pictilisib's FERGI toxicity stays on its own track (safety 4).

safety.model: PI3K-pathway-activated lines and xenografts (U87MG, IGROV-1; breast lines incl. MCF7, KPL-4, MDA-MB-361)
safety.quote: In part 1, grade 3 or worse adverse events occurred in 54 (61%) of 89 patients in the pictilisib group and 22 (28%) of 79 in the placebo group.
safety.note: Mice tolerated the effective pictilisib dose with normal weight gain; in FERGI 61% had grade 3+ events vs 28%, and part 2 cut the dose to 260 mg. Dated to FERGI part 1 at SABCS 2014 (abstract S2-02, reported 2014-12-10 by ASCO Post: grade 3+ rash 17%, diarrhoea 7%, more dose adjustments and discontinuations on the combination), the later side of the pairing (model 2009).
safety.short: Well tolerated in mice, not in FERGI
safety.confidence_note: Model side: Raynaud 2009 full text (PMC2718129), 'The therapy was well tolerated, and all groups of mice gained weight at similar rates to controls (data not shown).' Data not shown, so medium. FERGI abstract-level reading; whether the SABCS 2014 abstract reported adverse events was not verified, so the year is the 2016 epub.
safety.reason: Tolerated in mice, toxic in patients
safety.judgement: Passing tolerability claim scored as a safety prediction: the xenograft mice tolerated the effective dose, but breast cancer patients at the target exposure had more than twice the placebo rate of grade 3+ events (rash, diarrhoea, hyperglycaemia) and the dose was cut. Diarrhoea and weight loss are harms mice can show. Counted here, not in dose, because the model did not predict the harm.
